title: Secrets in Your Module: Offer Secret Inputs in Your Settings | Orchard Core
description:
A module that keeps a password or an API key in its settings has to invent its own way to store that value.

The Secrets module provides a secret input for settings screens. The user keeps the value in the settings, protected with Data Protection, or selects a secret of the Secrets module by name. Your module needs a reference to the Secrets abstractions, and no dependency on the Secrets feature.

In this video:
• What users get: the same field, with and without the Secrets feature
• Start with the abstractions: a reference, not a dependency
• Keep the value and the name: the settings of your module
• The display driver: create the editor model, and apply the posted one
• The view: render the editor with a tag helper
• Read the value at runtime: one call, with or without the Secrets feature
• Migrate Secrets: let users move a stored value to a secret
• Beyond site settings: the same steps for any stored credential

links.label: Adding secret support to your own credentials
